comparison: Perfect agreement on sample characteristics (C1, C29, C30, C38, C39, C40). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED and praise the large sample size, linguistic diversity, and use of replication sample.

Perfect agreement on partial replication (C5, C70, C71, C72, C73). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN, noting that only right hemisphere effects replicated while left hemisphere results were non-significant. Peer review explicitly criticizes lack of discussion about partial replication.

Agreement on single TTG subgroup analysis (C64-C69). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes small sample size limitation, while peer review implicitly accepts findings as part of praised segmentation methodology.

Agreement on genetic influences caveat (C93). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of limitation, while peer reviewers debate plausibility with one reviewer finding genetic explanation less likely than experience-based account.

Divergent evaluation of sample differences explanation (C103, C104). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding explanation reasonable. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, expressing concern about scanner differences and monolingual fraction not being adequately addressed.
Agreement on TASH methodology advantages (C120, C121, C124, C125). Both rate as SUPPORTED and praise the careful segmentation techniques for capturing anatomical variability.
Agreement on phonological vs. lexical specificity and hemispheric differences (C59, C60, C61). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly satisfied with lexical distance control analyses.

Strong agreement on main negative relationship finding (C2, C52, C57, C58). Both rate as SUPPORTED with high confidence. Editor and reviewers describe evidence as 'convincing' and 'solid,' matching OpenEval's assessment of consistent statistical support.
Agreement on typological distance measures (C7, C128, C129). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly satisfied with typological distance analyses as addressing potential confounds.

Agreement on exploratory PT findings (C48, C49, C94). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes later refinement to TTG specificity, while peer review praises comprehensive analysis of superior temporal cortex structure.
Agreement on TTG anatomy descriptive statistics (C50, C51, C63, C77, C91). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly praises segmentation techniques accounting for anatomical variability.

Divergent evaluation of plasticity interpretation (C6, C100, C105, C109-C111, C113). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanisms and cross-sectional design. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with editor stating findings 'strongly point to experience-dependent plasticity' and reviewers accepting interpretation.

Divergent evaluation of challenge to established models (C8, C96, C97-C99, C102). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative functional interpretation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, describing results as 'fascinating' and making 'compelling case' for linguistic experience shaping auditory cortex.

Agreement on phoneme-level model superiority (C3, C55, C56, C76, C92). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers highlight entropy measures and typological distance as strengths, with evidence for phoneme-level information being important.

Agreement on entropy-based methodology (C31, C32, C41). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly praises entropy measures for quantifying language experience and respecting linguistic diversity.

Agreement on functional neuroimaging support (C97, C98, C99). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes citations provide context but not direct demonstration, while peer review accepts these as part of compelling case for findings.

Partial overlap on interpretation of negative relationship (C4, C58, C62 vs C3, C4, C76, C92). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on converging evidence for interpretation, peer review emphasizes phoneme-level specificity as unlikely to emerge from aptitude.
Minimal overlap (C62). Both evaluations support related claims about hemispheric specificity and phonological effects, though addressing different aspects of the findings.

Partial overlap on anatomical specificity (C94, C95, C96). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to competing interpretations. Peer review implicitly accepts specificity findings as part of comprehensive analysis praised as strength.

Minimal overlap (C129). OpenEval rates interpretation of anatomical constraints as SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses typological distance more broadly, implicitly accepting anatomical specificity findings.

OpenEval rates vertex-wise analysis (C53, C54) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of multiple comparison correction. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this represents a methodological limitation.
OpenEval rates genetic contextualization (C22, C23, C90) as SUPPORTED, citing appropriate large-scale studies. No specific peer review evaluation of these background claims found.

OpenEval rates mechanistic interpretations of opposite direction effects (C91, C117-C119) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature. No specific peer review evaluation found, though related anatomical findings are accepted.

OpenEval rates typological distance methodology (C41-C47) as SUPPORTED with appropriate detail. Peer review praises entropy measures generally (R15) but does not specifically evaluate these methodological details.
OpenEval rates established anatomical background (C10-C15) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; background knowledge not typically evaluated by reviewers.
OpenEval rates HG background knowledge (C78-C84) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; background literature not specifically assessed.

OpenEval rates prior study interpretation (C28, C85, C86) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; literature review not specifically evaluated.
